prompt:
Normalize the single contact block in the user's note. Read only its label–value lines (labels vary; separators include colon, equals, tab). Ignore all surrounding text and signatures; do not fill values from email domains or company suffixes. Output only a bare JSON object with exactly name, phone, email, company, country, each a string or null.

Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent, blank, or whole-value placeholders (-, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD; any case) are null. Do not guess. The only fill-in is missing country from a unique international calling code.

Country comes from its own line when provided: map English, Swedish or German names and alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes, ignoring case, to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept common aliases: UK/Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA/U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.

Route other lines by content before label: @ means email; at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after stripping tel: and the extension means phone. For email strip mailto: and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address.

For phone strip leading tel: and any trailing extension in ext. N, ext N, xN, #N or extension N form (N is digits). International means leading + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. On that branch remove (0) before stripping spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses; replace leading 00 with + and keep the written calling code. A conflicting explicit country and international phone retain their own country and calling code respectively. If country is missing, use the international calling code's country only if unique (shared codes such as +1 and +7 give null). On the national branch, strip formatting, remove one leading trunk 0 if present, and prepend + and the resolved country's calling code; without country, return null. Phone strings must be E.164 (+ and digits only).

Legal suffixes (case-insensitive trailing matches): AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Swap name and company values if the name line ends in such a suffix and the company line does not. Then remove the company's trailing suffix and optional preceding comma, trim, and capitalize each space-separated word (first character uppercase, rest lowercase). For name, reverse Last, First at the first comma, drop leading Dr/Mr/Mrs/Ms/Mx/Prof (optional dot, any case), and capitalize each space- or hyphen-separated part the same way. Preserve all Unicode letters and diacritics when changing case; never transliterate.
